podcast.title: Discovery by Stiff Records
podcast.body: In 1978, the same year Kate Bush was making her chart debut, Lene Lovich attracted the attention of Stiff Records. This independent label was a prominent force in the punk and new wave music worlds at the time. "In 1978, around the very same time Kate Bush was debuting on the charts, Lena came to the attention of stiff records, an indie label very much at the forefront of the punk and new wave worlds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Diverse Artistic Background
podcast.body: Born in Troy, Lene Lovich pursued an education in art school in England, where she worked as a sculptor, actress, and cabaret performer. She also played the saxophone and contributed her screams for post-production on horror films, showcasing her eclectic talents before her music career took off. "She was born into Troy, but she ended up in art school in England working as a sculptor actress and a cabaret performer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Multi-Disciplinary Artistic Background
podcast.body: Born in Troy, Lene Lovich relocated to England, where she attended art school. There, she honed her skills as a sculptor and cabaret performer, in addition to playing the saxophone. She also contributed to film by lending her screams for post-production on horror films. "She was born into Troy, but she ended up in art school in England working as a sculptor and a cabaret performer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
